notes:
Traced from scratch (the bootstrap left 19 of 34 terminals null and its non-null guesses were not used). The sheet is drawn rotated ~90 deg, so every MOSFET gate bar runs horizontally. Coordinates are in the 512x512 frame.
NET MAP. 0 = the left vertical rail at x~91 (drifting to x~105 at the bottom), running y28->y505, plus everything GND touches: GND 4 taps it at (75,255); V-AC 3 left lead (via the top-left corner (91,28)->(148,20)), V-AC 6 left lead, MOSFET-N 8 source (left lead, y~230), MOSFET-P 5 source (left lead, y~383), I-AC 1 left lead (y~451), I-AC 0 left lead (y~503). The SECOND ground symbol, GND 13, sits under V-DC 2 and is fed by V-DC 2's bottom lead, so per the one-reference rule that net is also 0 - i.e. the left rail and the V-DC 2 return are one net named 0 even though they are drawn as separate wires with no ink between them. n1 = top line y~17 from V-AC 3 right lead to the Zener 9 anode, with a T at (214,19) dropping the x~215-225 column (the column drifts right as it descends): the column branches right at y~78 to the gate bar of MOSFET-P 7, and continues down past the crossover dip at (223,190) to the gate bar of MOSFET-N 14 (bar at y=214-215). n2 = the long mid horizontal at y~176: V-AC 6 right lead feeds it, the x~134 drop at its left end goes to the gate bar of MOSFET-N 8, and at its right end it turns down at x~387 to y~194 into the gate bar of MOSFET-N 11. n3 = horizontal y~228: drain (right lead) of MOSFET-N 8, top of Resistor 12 (T at (194,228)), source (left lead) of MOSFET-N 14. n4 = horizontal y~220-225: drain (right lead) of MOSFET-N 14 -> source (left lead) of MOSFET-N 11. n5 = the right vertical rail at x~427-440, y8->300: Zener 9 cathode, drain (right lead) of MOSFET-P 7, drain (right lead) of MOSFET-N 11, top lead of V-DC 2. n6 = source (left lead) of MOSFET-P 7 -> left along y~120 -> down the x~312 column (through the crossover dip at (312,187) and the crossing at (312,220)) -> y~375 -> left into the drain (right lead) of MOSFET-P 10. n7 = horizontal y~382 between MOSFET-P 5 and MOSFET-P 10: drain (right lead) of MOSFET-P 5, bottom of Resistor 12 (T at (205,382)), source (left lead) of MOSFET-P 10. n8 = gate of MOSFET-P 5: its gate bar (y~401) leads left, down at x~136, right along y~413 to x~202, down to y~451 and left into the right lead of I-AC 1. n9 = gate of MOSFET-P 10: gate bar y~398, lead down at x~291, then down/left to the right lead of I-AC 0 at y~503.
JUDGMENT CALLS. (a) CROSSOVER STYLE. This drafter marks a crossing by making the HORIZONTAL wire take a downward U-shaped detour whose lowest point grazes the crossed vertical; the vertical runs straight through at 1 px with no thickening. Verified in the raw bitmap at (223,190) and (312,187): in both the vertical is a continuous 1-2 px stroke through the whole window and the U is ~12 px deep. Both are CROSSINGS, so n2 joins neither n1 nor n6. (b) The crossing at (312,220), where the n4 horizontal meets the n6 column, carries NO dip and NO dot - a clean thin X (pixel map shows both strokes 1-2 px straight through, no local bulge). Read as a crossing, so n4 (MOSFET-N 14 drain / MOSFET-N 11 source) stays separate from n6. Both readings simulate, so nothing electrical forces the choice and the ink decides; this is the one call on the sheet a human should re-check, since the drafter does mark the other two crossings. (c) MOSFET-N 14: the n1 gate column comes down at x=225-226 and, 2 px BELOW the gate bar (bar at y=214-215), a separate stroke at x=225 runs from y=218 down to the n3 horizontal at y=228 - that stroke is MOSFET-N 14's left channel lead (source). The gate lead's 2 px overshoot at (226,216)-(226,217) touches the top of the source lead DIAGONALLY at (225,218), which merges them in a naive connected-component pass. It is a drawing artifact, not a connection: the same drafter leaves a clean 2-6 row gap between gate lead and channel in MOSFET-N 8 (gate lead ends y=210, channel starts y=216) and MOSFET-N 11 (gate lead ends y=197, channel starts y=204), and a gate lead is never wired to a channel lead. So n1 does NOT join n3, and MOSFET-N 14 has gate n1 / source n3 / drain n4. (d) MOSFET terminal roles: in every device the gate is the solid bar carrying the one lead perpendicular to the channel run (top for 7/8/11/14, bottom for the mirrored 5/10), and the channel bar is the three-segment bar. In each device the middle (bulk-arrow) lead merges with one outer lead; I called that merged pair the source and the lone lead the drain. Read at the pixel level for all six: 5 leads at x=138(ch)/148(bulk)/159 -> source 0, drain n7; 7 at x=366(ch)/375(bulk)/387 -> source n6, drain n5; 8 at x=128(ch)/137(bulk)/146 -> source 0, drain n3; 10 at x=295(ch)/304(bulk)/313 -> source n7, drain n6; 11 at x=390(ch)/401(bulk)/414 -> source n4, drain n5; 14 at x=225(ch)/231(bulk)/240 -> source n3, drain n4. Swapping D/S on any of them would not change the net partition. (e) Zener 9 is drawn with the triangle (anode) on the left at x~327-345 facing right into the barred cathode at x~346; anode = n1 (index 0), cathode = n5 (index 1). (f) Binarisation dropouts read as continuous, each a 1-3 row gap mid-run on a straight stroke with ink on both sides and the stroke resuming within 1 px in x: left rail at y=351, y=423, y=443, y=476-477; the n1 column at y=103-104, y=149-151 and y=179-181; the right rail at y=134, y=188 and y=277-279. Each was confirmed in the raw bitmap. (g) Resistor 12's bottom lead drops straight down at x~205 and T's onto the y~382 horizontal at a point that lies BETWEEN MOSFET-P 5 (bbox right edge x=169) and MOSFET-P 10 (bbox left edge x=282), so it joins the MOSFET-P-5-drain / MOSFET-P-10-source node (n7), not the MOSFET-P-10-drain node. Checked explicitly because the near-identical sheet circuit_963 has the analogous resistor landing on the other side of the lower P-MOSFET. (h) No component is off-frame: all 15 bbox centres lie inside 512x512 and every symbol is visible (I-AC 0's bbox reaches the bottom edge and V-AC 3's / Zener 9's reach the top edge, but the symbols themselves are fully drawn). Nothing was added, removed or re-classed, and no terminal is unconnected. (i) Tier-2 simcheck note: n8 and n9 have no DC path to ground - each is a current source (I-AC 1 / I-AC 0) driving an insulated MOSFET gate and nothing else. That is exactly what the ink shows: the wire out of each I-AC's right lead is a dead-end blob touching only that source and the one gate bar. Kept as drawn.
